CARES PostgreSQL Logical Transaction Boundaries (Round 1)

Status: Logical transaction-boundary analysis documented; NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT TESTED. This document describes proposed atomicity, idempotency, concurrency, and rollback expectations for future PostgreSQL design. It does not define executable SQL transactions, locking statements, isolation-level configuration, RLS policies, or exact-once external delivery guarantees. All controls described here are proposed unless explicitly established elsewhere and remain subject to technical/security/product/owner approval.

Global constraints and assumptions

  • Verified transaction-bound tenant context: tenant authority must be established from trusted verified context before tenant-scoped data operations; client-supplied tenant IDs and user-settable PostgreSQL GUC values are not authorization sources. RLS is defense in depth (future physical control).
  • Atomicity and durable idempotency: identity/licensing/lifecycle/history changes that must remain consistent require atomic persistence and durable idempotency/replay behavior as designed (e.g. identity_operation_idempotency_ledger, event_receipt for ingestion). Proposed contract (OD-008, approval required): identity/licensing idempotency uses tenant+operation type+idempotency key scope, deterministic request canonicalization/hash, and state outcomes in_progress/committed/failed_terminal/timeout_unknown_commit; same key + same canonical request must yield the original committed outcome (or explicit in-progress/unknown state) without duplicate assets, bindings, aliases, or licensed usage. Default recommendation for database-local identity/licensing operations is single-transaction coupling of ledger claim/state/result with business, audit/history/licensing, and required outbox records; staged multi-transaction tracking requires explicit leases/fencing/recovery (not default).
  • No competing source of truth (Round 1.1 recommendation, Proposed/OD-002 open): asset_data_source is the authoritative stable source-device binding entity and owns immutable source_device_key_id; any separately materialized source_device_key record must be a 1:1 dependent/non-authoritative projection with identical lifecycle and no competing attributes. source_device_fingerprint_alias records are versioned lookups to that same stable binding identity.
  • External side effects: network calls, provider transmissions, email/webhook/system actions outside PostgreSQL, and object-storage side effects that cannot be made transactionally atomic with DB commit must be coordinated via outbox/reconciliation/compensation patterns as designed; PostgreSQL transactions cannot guarantee exact-once external delivery.
  • Concurrency control: deterministic locking/order and post-lock rechecks are required for conflicting identity/licensing operations (proposed). Exact lock modes/rows are physical design concerns (Round 2+).

Operation-by-operation analysis

1. New canonical asset registration

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together asset (new canonical UUID), initial authoritative asset_data_source binding owning immutable source_device_key_id (and 1:1 dependent source_device_key projection only if modeled), initial source_device_fingerprint_alias and/or accepted asset_identity_claim provenance, asset_lifecycle_event, asset_license_event and/or usage/reservation transition, tenant_license_usage_state (or equivalent authoritative counters) as approved, identity_operation_idempotency_ledger claim/state/result, required audit_event(s), and any required outbox_message for downstream coordination (scope-dependent).
Required atomicity boundary Single database transaction for all required in-scope business state, idempotency outcome, audit records, and outbox records that must be consistent with commit/rollback of the registration decision (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Tenant-scoped unique canonical asset identity invariants; uniqueness preventing duplicate stable binding/key attachment and conflicting active bindings; tenant-scoped alias uniqueness over approved dimensions (no raw source IDs); quota/capacity consistency invariants; non-reusable canonical IDs.
Idempotency mechanism identity_operation_idempotency_ledger (Proposed contract): tenant + operation type + idempotency key, canonical request hash, in_progress→committed/terminal/timeout_unknown_commit semantics; same key+same request returns committed outcome, same key+different request conflicts. Default single-transaction coupling recommended for DB-local effects.
Expected rollback behavior On validation/conflict/quota failure or transaction abort: no partial asset, binding, alias, license counter, ledger-committed success result, or outbox side-effect record persists.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent registrations for same tenant/identity/quota can over-allocate or duplicate assets/bindings without serialized conflict control and post-lock rechecks.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Agent acknowledgments, notifications, external provisioning, or downstream non-DB actions must occur only after commit via safe coordination (outbox/worker) or be reconciled; not atomic with DB commit.
Decisions that remain unresolved Quota accounting equation (active/reserved/pending/available), reservation policy, authoritative counter representation, exact lock ordering, connector/identity authority rules (owner/technical approvals).

2. Existing asset attachment from another data source

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together Resolved asset association (no new licensed asset), new or attached authoritative asset_data_source binding (owning immutable source_device_key_id) and dependent key projection only if modeled, required alias/claim provenance updates, asset_lifecycle_event, identity_operation_idempotency_ledger claim/state/result, audit_event, and optional outbox; licensed usage must not increase for attaching additional source to already-resolved unique device.
Required atomicity boundary Single transaction for binding/provenance/history/idempotency/audit/outbox consistency (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Unique authoritative resolution to exactly one canonical asset; prevent duplicate active binding for same stable source-device context; one data source may have many device bindings; no cross-tenant attachment.
Idempotency mechanism Identity/licensing operation idempotency ledger for the attachment operation/request key.
Expected rollback behavior No duplicate binding/alias/provenance side effects or false license increment on failure.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent attach vs merge/split/deactivation or conflicting identity resolution can create inconsistent bindings if not serialized/rechecked.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Post-commit notifications/sync to external systems via outbox if needed.
Decisions that remain unresolved Approval of binding ownership recommendation (OD-002), authoritative match rules by connector namespace, handling of late-arriving conflicting claims.

3. Source-device fingerprint alias creation

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together New source_device_fingerprint_alias linked to existing stable source_device_key/binding context, provenance/audit and optional lifecycle metadata, and idempotency/result record when operation is externally retriable as a managed operation.
Required atomicity boundary Transaction ensuring alias uniqueness, stable-binding linkage, and audit/idempotency consistency for the creation action (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Tenant-scoped uniqueness over approved dimensions (tenant, data-source/binding context, algorithm, key version, protected fingerprint); no raw source ID keys; alias must resolve to same binding only.
Idempotency mechanism Operation idempotency ledger for managed alias-creation requests; natural uniqueness can also prevent duplicates but replay must return consistent outcome.
Expected rollback behavior No orphan/duplicate alias or ambiguous resolution state on failure.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent alias creation/rotation for same key may violate uniqueness or create conflicting active states without coordination.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction None required by default; any cache invalidation/notification external to DB must be reconciled post-commit.
Decisions that remain unresolved Approved uniqueness dimensions, overlap window rules, who/what may trigger alias creation.

4. Fingerprint key/algorithm rotation

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together New alias/version material for same stable source_device_key/binding, overlap validity state for old/new aliases, rotation control/audit records, and idempotency outcome; retirement of old aliases/keys by controlled transition (may be staged but consistency-critical steps atomic).
Required atomicity boundary Each controlled rotation step that changes lookup/validity invariants must be atomic (proposed); multi-step rotation workflows require idempotent, resumable state transitions and reconciliation.
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints No duplicate aliases violating dimensions; all active/overlapping aliases for same rotation context resolve to same stable binding/asset; stable binding identity unchanged.
Idempotency mechanism Rotation operation/request idempotency ledger and/or deterministic step identifiers.
Expected rollback behavior Failed step leaves no inconsistent alias state that maps to different bindings/assets or breaks resolvability guarantees.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent rotation, lookup, and registration/attach operations can observe mixed states; requires coordination and post-lock rechecks.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Cryptographic key management/HSM/KMS operations, re-fingerprinting jobs, and downstream cache updates are external and must be reconciled; DB cannot atomically include them.
Decisions that remain unresolved Key custody/rotation authority, overlap duration, migration tooling, emergency rotation procedures (owner/security approval).

5. Identity conflict and pending resolution

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together identity_resolution_case creation/update, linkage of conflicting/ambiguous asset_identity_claim(s)/binding candidates, quarantine/pending state markers as designed, optional asset_license_reservation create/update per approved policy, lifecycle/audit records, idempotency outcome, and optional outbox notification.
Required atomicity boundary Case state, claim linkages, and any reservation/accounting effect required by policy must be committed consistently (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Prevent auto-merge/auto-create of duplicate canonical asset when conflict/ambiguity exists; reservation must not be double-counted; case must remain tenant-scoped.
Idempotency mechanism Idempotency ledger for resolution workflow operations and/or deterministic case-creation keys for same evidence context.
Expected rollback behavior No partial pending state that leaks unresolved data into normal analysis or double-reserves capacity.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent ingestion events may generate duplicate/conflicting cases or race with manual resolution; requires dedupe/locking strategy.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Analyst notifications, ticketing, or external workflow systems via outbox/integration; not atomic.
Decisions that remain unresolved Pending quarantine behavior, reservation-per-case default, expiry, reject-vs-hold policy, and who can resolve (owner/security/commercial).

6. Asset merge

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together asset_merge_operation record, survivor/loser state transitions, reassignment of eligible asset_data_source bindings and associated source_device_fingerprint_alias (preserving single authoritative binding identity, no competing source of truth), asset_identity_claim/case link updates, typed asset_lineage_link records (typed FKs to assets and merge operation, no polymorphic refs), asset_lifecycle_event, asset_license_event and tenant_license_usage_state adjustments per approved accounting (no duplicate licensed usage), tombstone/terminal handling for losing canonical assets, identity_operation_idempotency_ledger claim/state/result, audit_event, and required outbox.
Required atomicity boundary Entire merge effect set that must be consistent (identity reassignment, lineage, licensing/accounting, audit, idempotency) in one transaction or in a strictly controlled compensatable workflow if technically impossible—but DB-authoritative state transitions should be atomic where feasible (proposed). Prefer single-transaction logical boundary.
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Explicit survivor; losing canonical IDs never reused; bindings/aliases must not end up attached to multiple assets; typed lineage FKs preserve referential integrity and tenant consistency; tenant-inclusive integrity preserved; no cross-tenant merge.
Idempotency mechanism Merge operation idempotency key/ledger; repeated submit returns committed merge outcome.
Expected rollback behavior Full rollback on conflict/validation/capacity/integrity failure with no partial reassignment or accounting drift.
Concurrency/race-condition risk High: concurrent merges/splits/attach/ingest/license updates can corrupt lineage or licensing without deterministic locking and conflict checks.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Search index updates, notifications, external system sync—post-commit/reconciled.
Decisions that remain unresolved Merge approval authority/evidence, accounting effects, handling of in-flight events and historical attribution display rules.

7. Asset split

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together asset_split_operation record, creation of new canonical asset UUID when justified, movement of specified asset_data_source bindings and their aliases/claims (stable binding identity preserved per authoritative model), typed asset_lineage_link records (typed FKs to assets and split operation), lifecycle/license events, capacity/quota verification and any reservation/usage changes required if additional active billable asset is created (policy-dependent), tombstone/state updates for source context as applicable, identity_operation_idempotency_ledger claim/state/result, audit, and outbox.
Required atomicity boundary Single transaction for split decision, identity movement, lineage, and licensing/capacity effects that must not diverge (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints No duplication of binding/alias ownership; original attribution/history preserved; canonical ID non-reuse; quota/capacity checks atomic before commit when needed.
Idempotency mechanism Split operation idempotency ledger.
Expected rollback behavior No orphan new asset, no partial binding moves, no incorrect licensed usage increment/decrement.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent split with merge/attach/registration/quota changes; risk of double allocation or lost bindings.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Downstream re-indexing/notifications external to DB.
Decisions that remain unresolved When split creates billable asset vs reservation conversion, approval authority, evidence standards, quota-at-split policy.

8. Asset deactivation/reactivation/removal

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together asset lifecycle state transition, asset_lifecycle_event, binding/source state updates as applicable, asset_license_event and tenant_license_usage_state/reservation/tombstone effects per approved policy, idempotency ledger, audit, and outbox.
Required atomicity boundary State transition and any associated licensing/accounting/history effects that must remain consistent committed together (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Canonical ID remains stable/non-reusable; removal must not delete required history/tombstone lineage; deactivation must not be conflated with source disconnection unless policy states so.
Idempotency mechanism Lifecycle operation idempotency ledger/request keys.
Expected rollback behavior No half-applied lifecycle/licensing state.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent lifecycle operations, merges, or new attachments/resolution outcomes.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Agent disablement, archival jobs, external notifications—coordinated post-commit.
Decisions that remain unresolved Grace periods, quota release timing, permanent removal authorization, retention/legal hold interaction (owner/legal/privacy/security).

9. Asset quota allocation/reservation/release

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together subscription_entitlement reference/validation context (read), tenant_license_usage_state counter transitions, optional asset_license_reservation and/or asset_license_event, linked asset/case/operation context, idempotency ledger, and audit.
Required atomicity boundary Capacity check and counter/reservation mutation must be atomic to prevent over-allocation or double-counting (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Active/reserved/pending/available semantics consistent and non-double-counting; tenant-scoped capacity isolation.
Idempotency mechanism Identity/licensing operation idempotency ledger for allocate/reserve/release/convert actions.
Expected rollback behavior No leaked reservation or inflated/deflated counters on failure.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Core contention point: concurrent allocations/releases/conversions/merges/splits require serialized checks.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Billing system synchronization, customer notifications—outside DB transaction, reconciled via outbox/process controls if implemented.
Decisions that remain unresolved Commercial accounting equation, reservation inclusion in counters, expiry/release rules, billing treatment (owner/commercial).

10. Event ingestion acceptance

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together event_receipt (durable dedupe outcome with explicit namespace/provenance), accepted security_event record when applicable, and required outbox_message(s) for downstream processing—persisted atomically for accepted path as designed; audit/metrics metadata as required.
Required atomicity boundary Receipt + accepted event + outbox creation must be committed together so acknowledged ingestion is durable and processable without duplication/loss of coordination (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Unique logical dedupe scope per tenant_id + explicit dedup_namespace_type + dedup_namespace_id + normalized source_event_key (proposed), enforced via receipt ledger. Namespace selection must prevent cross-device collisions: data-source-global ID => tenant+data_source_id; device-scoped ID => tenant+stable source-device binding identity (asset_data_source/source_device_key_id context); unreliable/missing ID => deterministic approved fallback or reject/quarantine (Open Decision). Same key/same payload returns prior result; same key/different payload conflicts as policy defines. Raw source identifiers never used as DB uniqueness keys.
Idempotency mechanism event_receipt is the ingestion idempotency mechanism (distinct from identity/licensing ledger).
Expected rollback behavior No acknowledged-but-unrecorded event; on rejection/conflict/validation failure, no partial accepted-event/outbox state inconsistent with receipt outcome.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Duplicate deliveries/retries and concurrent writers for same key; partitioned event storage cannot replace global receipt uniqueness.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Source acknowledgment over network occurs at API boundary but must reflect durable commit outcome; downstream processing is asynchronous via outbox/worker.
Decisions that remain unresolved Connector-specific namespace capability/fallback rules for unreliable/missing upstream IDs (OD/open), payload-hash/conflict policy details, retention of receipts vs events, backpressure behavior thresholds (owner/ops/performance).

11. Outbox claim and processing

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together outbox_message claim/lease/fence state transition, outbox_attempt (or equivalent metadata) creation/update, processing state/result references, and any tenant-scoped derived business updates produced by processing (alerts/case updates/etc.) as one or more well-defined transactions per consistency boundary.
Required atomicity boundary Claim acquisition and attempt-state updates must be atomic to prevent unsafe double-claim; business side effects of processing should be committed with completion state according to designed unit-of-work boundaries (proposed).
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Lease/fencing token or equivalent monotonic claim guard to prevent stale workers committing results; message state machine integrity.
Idempotency mechanism Processing handlers must be idempotent where retries/duplicate delivery possible; attempt/replay metadata supports safe reprocessing decisions.
Expected rollback behavior On worker failure before completion commit, claim/attempt state reflects retryable outcome without marking business effects complete.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Competing workers, lease expiry races, and zombie worker commits; mitigated by fencing/leases (proposed).
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Any external call performed during processing (webhooks, notifications, provider APIs) is outside DB atomicity and must be represented via outbox/reconciliation semantics.
Decisions that remain unresolved Lease durations, max attempts, dead-letter policy, fencing implementation details (TD-008).

12. Outbox external delivery with unknown outcome

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together outbox_attempt/message state transition to delivery_unknown (or equivalent), diagnostic/reconciliation metadata, correlation identifiers, and audit/operational records needed to prevent unsafe blind replay.
Required atomicity boundary Persisting unknown-outcome state and reconciliation markers must be atomic so operators/workers see a consistent ambiguity state.
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Must not silently convert unknown outcome to success/failure without evidence; replay controls tied to idempotency/fencing.
Idempotency mechanism External endpoint idempotency keys (where supported) and internal reconciliation workflow; no assumption of exactly-once external delivery.
Expected rollback behavior If ambiguity state cannot be durably recorded, fail-safe handling required (no false completion).
Concurrency/race-condition risk Reconciliation job and retry worker may race; fencing/state checks required.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction The external delivery itself is the side effect with unknown commit/ack outcome; reconciliation may require external status queries.
Decisions that remain unresolved Reconciliation ownership/SLA, retry ceilings, manual intervention criteria, external idempotency capabilities by integration.

13. Forensic evidence creation and controlled transition

Aspect Logical analysis
Records that must change together forensic_evidence_record metadata, initial evidence_object_version reference metadata (hash/locator/size/integrity attributes as applicable), initial evidence_custody_event, linkage to case/asset/tenant context, required audit records, and any evidence_transition_authorization for controlled transitions (when required).
Required atomicity boundary DB metadata/custody/authorization state that must be consistent with evidence registration or transition decision should commit atomically (proposed). Object bytes stored outside PostgreSQL cannot be in the same DB transaction.
Relevant uniqueness/integrity constraints Immutable version identity/integrity hashes; append-only custody history; tenant/case scoping; separation from operational audit.
Idempotency mechanism Evidence ingestion/registration operation idempotency keys to prevent duplicate logical records for retried uploads/requests (proposed).
Expected rollback behavior If metadata commit fails, no false claim of preserved/custodied evidence; orphan external objects require reconciliation/cleanup process outside transaction.
Concurrency/race-condition risk Concurrent uploads/transitions/legal-hold actions; requires controlled state machine and authorization checks.
External side effects outside PostgreSQL transaction Object storage write/read/delete, WORM storage controls, legal-hold systems, and cross-system replication are external side effects with independent failure modes.
Decisions that remain unresolved Storage/WORM commitments, retention/legal-hold/deletion authority, transition approval policy, integrity verification cadence (owner/legal/compliance/security).

Cross-operation notes

  • Idempotency taxonomy: ingestion uses event_receipt (explicit dedup namespace/provenance, device-collision-safe by design); licensing/identity operations use identity_operation_idempotency_ledger (proposed contract: scope/key/hash, in-progress/committed/failed/unknown states, default single-transaction coupling for DB-local effects); outbox uses attempt/replay/fencing metadata. These mechanisms are related but distinct.
  • Compensation vs rollback: database rollback applies only within transaction boundaries; external effects require compensating actions/reconciliation and must not be represented as rolled-back DB state.
  • Performance/SLO assumptions: no production performance or latency commitment is established by this logical analysis.

Round 1.1 consistency notes (proposed, not approved)

  • Binding model: transactions assume the recommended authoritative asset_data_source ownership of stable binding identity (source_device_key_id) with 1:1 dependent/non-authoritative key projection only if materialized (OD-002 approval required).
  • Identity/licensing idempotency contract: default recommendation is single-transaction coupling for database-local operations; staged tracking requires explicit leases/fencing/recovery. Unknown-commit outcomes require reconciliation and must not be treated as blind success/failure. No exactly-once external delivery is claimed.
  • Lineage integrity: merge/split lineage must use typed, relationally enforceable references (typed asset and operation FKs) rather than generic polymorphic references.
  • Event dedup namespace: explicit namespace prevents cross-device collisions for multi-device connectors when upstream IDs are device-scoped; connector-specific unreliable/missing-ID handling remains open where not yet defined.
